sites.quote: For that purpose, the requirement level for 128-bit keys and 256-bit keys is MUST (when applicable).
In that sense, the status for 256-bit keys has been raised from MAY in [RFC7321] to MUST.
sites.reason: restates for 256-bit keys the key-length MUST of the previous sentence

sites.quote: These algorithms were not mentioned in [RFC7321], and this document clarifies that such algorithms MUST NOT be implemented for IPsec communications.
As a result, these algorithms MUST NOT be implemented.
Various ciphers that are older, not well tested, and never widely implemented have been changed to MUST NOT.
ENCR_BLOWFISH has been downgraded to MUST NOT as it has been deprecated for years by TWOFISH, which is not standardized for ESP and therefore not listed in this document.
ENCR_NULL status was set to MUST in [RFC7321] and remains a MUST to enable the use of ESP with only authentication, which is preferred over AH due to NAT traversal.
ENCR_NULL is expected to remain MUST by protocol requirements.
sites.reason: predicts that ENCR_NULL stays MUST; the grade itself is the previous sentence

sites.quote: ENCR_AES_CBC status remains at MUST.
sites.reason: the ENCR_AES_CBC MUST is graded by the next sentence of Section 5

sites.quote: ENCR_AES_CBC MUST be implemented in order to enable interoperability between implementations that followed [RFC7321].
ENCR_AES_GCM_16 status has been updated from SHOULD+ to MUST in order to favor the use of authenticated encryption and AEAD algorithms.
Its status has been set to SHOULD and is expected to become MUST in the long term.
sites.reason: the enclosing construction is "Its status has been set to SHOULD and is expected to become MUST in the long term": the capitalised MUST names the level the algorithm held in the obsoleted RFC or the level it may reach later; the grade the sentence assigns today is advisory

sites.quote: o Communications that are encrypted with a non-AEAD algorithm that MUST be combined with an authentication algorithm.
sites.reason: restates the Section 4 rule that a non-AEAD cipher needs an integrity algorithm
the Section 6 table; each graded row is captured by the prose sentences that follow it

sites.quote: AUTH_NONE has been downgraded from MAY in [RFC7321] to MUST NOT.
In all other cases, AUTH_NONE MUST NOT be selected.
As MD5 is known to be vulnerable to collisions, these algorithms MUST NOT be used.
AUTH_HMAC_SHA1_96 has been downgraded from MUST in [RFC7321] to MUST- as there is an industry-wide trend to deprecate its usage.
As DES is known to be vulnerable, it MUST NOT be used.
AUTH_HMAC_SHA2_256_128 MUST be implemented in order to replace AUTH_HMAC_SHA1_96.

sites.reason: "As it is not widely deployed, it remains optional and at the MAY level.": the IPCOMP_OUI MUST NOT grades a compression transform, and ze negotiates no IPComp transform for a Child SA (internal/component/ike/crypto/transform.go holds no compression registry). The absent compression is disclosed on docs/features/rfc-status.md through the Support remaining row of rfc/short/rfc8221.md
